info.name: PayLedger API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the PayLedger backend API -- every route actually registered in `apps/backend/src/routes/v1`, generated from the real Express routers and Zod validators, not hand-maintained.

### Base URL
`http://localhost:5001/api/v1` (`{{baseUrl}}`); `{{serverUrl}}` is the bare origin, used only by `/health`.

### Authentication architecture
- **User & admin are fully separate**: separate tables (`users` vs `admins`), separate session tables (`user_sessions` vs `admin_sessions`), separate auth guards (`requireUserAuth` / `requireAdminAuth`), and -- important if you're testing both in the same Postman cookie jar -- **separate cookie names**:
  - User: `access_token` / `refresh_token`
  - Admin: `admin_access_token` / `admin_refresh_token`
  (These used to share the same cookie names, which meant logging into one silently logged the other out in the same browser/cookie jar -- fixed by giving admin sessions their own names.)
- **Cookies, not tokens, in the body**: both access and refresh tokens are HttpOnly cookies, `SameSite=Lax`, scoped by `path=/`. They are **never** present in any JSON response body. Postman's cookie jar handles this automatically as long as requests in a folder run against the same `{{baseUrl}}` in sequence (Login, then everything else).
- **Access tokens**: short-lived (~15m) stateless JWTs.
- **Refresh tokens**: long-lived (~30d), stored hashed (SHA-256) in Postgres, rotated on every `/refresh`, with replay detection -- presenting an already-rotated-away refresh token revokes the whole session immediately, not just that one request.

### Idempotency
Every financial state-mutating endpoint (`POST /payments`, `POST /transfers`, `POST /withdrawals`) requires an `Idempotency-Key` header with a valid UUID. A repeated key against the same endpoint returns the original record rather than creating a duplicate -- safe to retry on a network timeout.

### Monetary units
Request and response bodies use **INR** (rupees, decimals allowed) everywhere *except* the payment gateway webhook's `amount` field, which is **paise** (integer) to match the gateway's own wire format -- ₹500 is sent as `50000`. Internally everything is stored as integer paise (`BIGINT`).

### Business/reference IDs
`orderId` (`ORD`-prefixed), the gateway's `paymentId` (`PAY`-prefixed), and every `referenceId` (transactions/transfers/withdrawals, unprefixed) are a 13-character Snowflake-derived Base32hex string, e.g. `ORD02QC3C3D00000` / `PAY02QC3BDDK0000` / `02QB4HB9O0000` -- never a raw UUID. Primary key `id` fields *are* UUIDs, but neither frontend ever renders those as visible text.

### A note on FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED payments
`GET /transactions` is a ledger of actual money movements -- a payment that never completed doesn't belong there, since nothing moved. Use `GET /payments` to see every deposit attempt regardless of outcome; it's the only place a failed deposit stays visible after the fact. The same isn't true for transfers: a rejected transfer never persists any row at all (every business-rule check happens before the first write, inside one DB transaction), so there's nothing to "lose" -- the failure is only ever the immediate response to `POST /transfers`.

item.name: User - Authentication
item.description: Register, log in, inspect the current session, refresh, and log out as a regular user.

request.description:
Registers a new user, creates their wallet (0 balance), starts a session, and writes an audit log -- all in one atomic DB transaction.

### Validation
- **name**: 2-100 characters.
- **mobile**: valid 10-digit Indian mobile number (`^[6-9]\d{9}$`).
- **email**: optional, valid email, max 255 characters.
- **password**: 8-128 characters.

### Cookies set
- `access_token` (HttpOnly, ~15m)
- `refresh_token` (HttpOnly, ~30d)

response.name: 409 Conflict - duplicate mobile/email
422 Validation error

request.description:
Authenticates a user by mobile number + Argon2id password check.

### Security
- **Anti-enumeration**: identical `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for a missing mobile or a wrong password.
- **Account lockout**: 5 failed attempts locks the account for 15 minutes.
- **Rate limited** via Redis (`auth:login`).

### Cookies set
- `access_token` (HttpOnly, ~15m)
- `refresh_token` (HttpOnly, ~30d)

Returns the authenticated user's own profile.

### Auth
Requires a valid `access_token` cookie.

Rotates the access + refresh token pair using the `refresh_token` cookie.

### Replay protection
If an already-consumed (rotated-away) refresh token is presented, the entire session is revoked immediately -- not just this request rejected.

### Cookies set
- New rotated `access_token` and `refresh_token`
Logs out idempotently: revokes the session server-side and clears both auth cookies regardless of whether a valid session existed.

item.name: User - Wallet
item.description: View the authenticated user's own balance, held amount, and available spendable funds.

request.description:
Fetches the authenticated user's own wallet summary.

### Fields
- **balance**: total ledger balance (INR).
- **held**: reserved for pending withdrawals (INR).
- **available**: `balance - held`, the actually spendable amount (INR).

### Auth
Requires a valid `access_token` cookie.

Lists every deposit attempt the authenticated user has made, regardless of status -- including FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED ones, which never create a `transactions` row (no money moved) and so are otherwise invisible once you navigate away from the in-progress checkout screen. This is the *only* place to see a failed deposit after the fact.

- `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100)
- `status` optional filter

request.description:
Initiates a deposit order with the Fake Payment Gateway. The row is created `CREATED`, then the gateway is called (outside any open DB transaction, so a slow/failed upstream call never holds a row lock) -- on gateway failure the payment is marked `FAILED` immediately, never left dangling.

### Validation
- **amount**: positive INR, between `PAYMENT_MIN_DEPOSIT_INR` (100) and `PAYMENT_MAX_DEPOSIT_INR` (25000).
- **Idempotency-Key**: required UUID header -- a repeated key returns the original payment, never creates a second one.

header.description: Required unique UUID to guarantee idempotent processing of this request

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - amount out of range

header.description: Required unique UUID to guarantee idempotent processing of this request

request.description: Fetches one payment belonging to the authenticated user. 404s (never leaks existence) for another user's payment.

Drives the Fake Payment Gateway's own test-checkout action -- the only way to move a CREATED/PROCESSING payment to a terminal state in this environment, since the gateway has no hosted checkout page. This never sets the payment's status directly: it only triggers the gateway, which then calls PayLedger's real signed `/payments/webhook` to actually complete it (same code path as a real provider).

### Body
- `outcome`: `SUCCESS` or `FAILED`
- `reason`: optional string, used when `outcome` is `FAILED`

response.name: 409 Conflict - already terminal

header.value: <hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, using PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET>

request.description:
Receives completion callbacks from the Fake Payment Gateway. Never guarded by `requireUserAuth` -- authenticated purely by the HMAC signature, verified over the *exact raw request bytes*, never a re-serialized copy.

### Body
- `orderId` / `paymentId`: strings (both now `ORD`-/`PAY`-prefixed business IDs, not UUIDs)
- `status`: `SUCCESS` or `FAILED`
- `amount`: **paise**, not INR (₹500 = 50000)
- `failureReason`: optional, present when `status` is `FAILED`

### What happens on SUCCESS
Credits the wallet, creates a balanced DEPOSIT transaction + ledger entries, and marks the payment `SUCCESS` -- all in one DB transaction, with the payment row locked `FOR UPDATE` so a duplicate/concurrent delivery of the same webhook is a safe no-op, never a double credit.

### What happens on FAILED
Marks the payment `FAILED` with the given reason. **No transaction row is created** -- nothing moved, so this never appears in `/transactions`. Use `GET /payments` to see it.

item.name: User - Transfers
item.description: Peer-to-peer wallet transfers between registered PayLedger users.

request.description: Looks up a transfer recipient by Indian mobile number before sending money. Rejects a self-lookup, and never reveals anything about a recipient whose wallet isn't eligible beyond a plain not-found.

header.description: Required unique UUID to guarantee idempotent processing of this request

request.description:
Transfers funds directly to another user's wallet with a zero-sum, immutable double-entry ledger. All rejections (insufficient balance, blocked wallet, self-transfer, over any limit) throw synchronously inside one DB transaction -- **no row is ever persisted for a rejected transfer**, so the failure surfaces immediately in this response, never as a silent/invisible record to look up later.

### Business rules
- Max single transfer: `TRANSFER_MAX_AMOUNT_INR` (₹25,000).
- Daily rolling limit: `TRANSFER_DAILY_LIMIT_INR` (₹50,000), counted in IST calendar days.
- System fee: 1% (min ₹1, max ₹20), credited to the system wallet.
- Wallets are locked in a fixed UUID order (never sender/receiver role order) to prevent deadlocks.

### Idempotency-Key
Required UUID header -- a repeated key returns the original transfer.

request.description:
Reverses a COMPLETED transfer: debits the receiver and credits the sender exactly the original amount (the fee is **not** refunded -- it stays with the system wallet). Creates a new TRANSFER_REVERSAL transaction; never mutates the original. Wallets are locked in a fixed UUID order to prevent deadlocks against another reversal/transfer on the same pair. Writes an audit log recording the authenticated admin, always from the session -- never from the request body.

### Rules
- Only a `COMPLETED` transfer can be reversed.
- Rejects if the receiver's *available* balance can't cover giving the amount back.

response.name: 409 Conflict - already reversed
409 Conflict - not completed
